title: Smale’s seventh problem
formal: Do there exist constants C,K>0, an integer k≥1 and a deterministic real-number algorithm A in the model below such that, for every integer N≥2, A(N) outputs N distinct points x₁,…,x_N on S² in at most KN^k operations and E_N(x₁,…,x_N)≤E_N*+C ln N?

definitions: S²={x∈ℝ³: x₁²+x₂²+x₃²=1}. The energy is E_N(x₁,…,x_N)=Σ_{i≠j}−ln‖x_i−x_j‖₂, counting ordered pairs; collisions have energy +∞. E_N* is the infimum over all N-tuples on S². ln is the natural logarithm and ‖·‖₂ is Euclidean distance. The algorithm is one finite real-arithmetic program with a fixed finite list of real constants, independent of N. It has exact real registers and a finite-control tape machine with register copying, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero register, and branching on the sign of a register. Tape movements and each scalar arithmetic, comparison or copy operation have unit cost. Input is the integer N as an exact real value; output is a list of 3N real coordinates. Any finite tape/register storage used by the program is charged through its operations. There is no primitive logarithm, square root, floor, random sample or minimization oracle. Polynomial time is in N, not in log N. The inequality is a mathematical condition on the output; the algorithm need not evaluate the energy. This specifies the real-number computation convention in Smale’s problem; coordinates need not be rational and no bit-cost bound is asserted.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: Smale's seventh problem concerns placing N points on the unit sphere so that their logarithmic interaction energy is nearly minimal.
The target is an algorithm running in time polynomial in N.
Its output energy may exceed the global minimum by only a universal constant times log N.
This is an additive energy guarantee, which requires more precise control than merely producing visually well-distributed points.
A construction with a rigorous bound would connect efficient computation with the equilibrium behavior of many mutually repelling particles on a curved surface.
